title: Failure Domains
reward: Learn where failure can originate before assigning intent.
knowledge: Separate cloud edge, host route, overlay, reverse proxy, container and application failure domains.
No proxy log can mean a different failure class than proxy 502.
502/504 suggest upstream/reachability/latency investigation, not hostile-client proof.
Listener absence, firewall drop and application error are distinct observations.
Resource pressure can be cause, consequence or unrelated coincidence.
Before identity reasoning, inspect real interface traffic and distinguish inbound/RX from outbound/TX at the observation point.
Distinguish port, socket, listener and established connection, and map them to the owning process when evidence is available.
Relate host sockets to containers and network namespaces instead of treating bridge addresses as external identities.
Trace topology through reverse proxy, NAT, hairpin NAT, overlay and container networking before attributing identity.
Only after the transport path is understood may identity or anomalous behavior be inferred, with uncertainty kept explicit.
challenge: Trace one observed flow from interface RX/TX through a listener or connection to a process or container, and state the observation boundary.
Explain how NAT, hairpin or a reverse proxy can change what source address is observed before any identity claim.
Trace one failure through at least three possible domains while keeping intent undecided when evidence is operational only.
next_requires: Demonstrate practical interface/socket/process/container/topology reasoning before Identity Through Boundaries.
